PROBLEM STATEMENT : ( Tourism Project)¶

The company "Visit with us" is looking to expand its customer base by introducing a new Wellness Tourism Package. Currently, they offer five types of packages: Basic, Standard, Deluxe, Super Deluxe, and King. However, only 18% of customers purchased these packages last year, and identifying potential customers has been challenging due to random contact methods. Wellness Tourism focuses on promoting a healthy lifestyle and well-being. The Data Scientist is tasked with analyzing customer data to identify the right target audience for the new package. It is also expected to build a predictive model that will help forecast which customers are likely to purchase the new product, thus allowing the company to contact only those who show potential interest.

#Examine the outliers using IQR (Interquartile Range)
Q1 = df['NumberOfPersonVisiting'].quantile(0.25)
Q3 = df['NumberOfPersonVisiting'].quantile(0.75)
IQR = Q3 - Q1
# Calculate the lower and upper bounds
lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
print(f"Lower Bound: {lower_bound}")
print(f"Upper Bound: {upper_bound}")
#Identify the outliers
outliers = df[(df['NumberOfPersonVisiting'] < lower_bound) | (df['NumberOfPersonVisiting'] > upper_bound)]
print("\nOutliers in NumberOfPersonVisiting:")
print(outliers)
#Impute the outliers with the median (or another method like capping)
# You can choose median, mean, or cap them at the lower or upper bound
median_value = df['NumberOfPersonVisiting'].median()
# Imputing the outliers with the median value
df['NumberOfPersonVisiting'] = np.where((df['NumberOfPersonVisiting'] < lower_bound) | (df['NumberOfPersonVisiting'] > upper_bound), median_value, df['NumberOfPersonVisiting'])
# Display the data after imputation
print("\nData after imputing the outliers:")
print(df)

sns.pairplot(df[numerical_cols])

plt.show()
#Multivariate Analysis - Correlation Heatmap
correlation_matrix = df[numerical_cols].corr()
sns.heatmap(correlation_matrix, annot=True, cmap='coolwarm', fmt='.2f', linewidths=0.5)

Observations:


Age: The mean and median age of customers who purchased each package. For example, we may find that younger people tend to buy Basic or Standard packages, while older customers tend to prefer King or Super Deluxe packages.


MonthlyIncome: The average income across different packages can give insights into which package is more popular among high-income or low-income customers. Higher-end packages like Deluxe, Super Deluxe, and King might attract people with a higher income, while Basic or Standard might attract a more budget-conscious demographic.


NumberOfTrips: we can compare how frequently people who purchased different packages travel. Those who purchase more expensive packages might take more trips overall.


NumberOfFollowups: This could indicate how often customers needed to be followed up with in the sales process. A higher number of follow-ups might indicate that customers purchasing certain packages are harder to convert.

Cost Complexity Pruning for Decision Tree


















In [62]:






path = dt_classifier.cost_complexity_pruning_path(X_train, Y_train)
ccp_alphas = path.ccp_alphas
impurities = path.impurities
train_accuracies = []
test_accuracies = []
for alpha in ccp_alphas:
    dt_pruned = DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=42, ccp_alpha=alpha)
    dt_pruned.fit(X_train, Y_train)
    train_accuracies.append(dt_pruned.score(X_train, Y_train))
    test_accuracies.append(dt_pruned.score(X_test, Y_test))
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(ccp_alphas, train_accuracies, label="Train Accuracy", marker='o')
plt.plot(ccp_alphas, test_accuracies, label="Test Accuracy", marker='o')
plt.xlabel('Alpha')
plt.ylabel('Accuracy')
plt.title('Cost Complexity Pruning - Train and Test Accuracy')
plt.legend()
plt.show()
best_alpha = ccp_alphas[np.argmax(test_accuracies)]
print(f"Best alpha: {best_alpha}")

dt_classifier = DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=42)
rf_classifier = RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42)
bagging_classifier = BaggingClassifier(random_state=42)
ada_boost_classifier = AdaBoostClassifier(random_state=42)
gradient_boosting_classifier = GradientBoostingClassifier(random_state=42)
xgb_classifier = XGBClassifier(random_state=42, use_label_encoder=False, eval_metric='logloss')
dt_classifier.fit(X_train, Y_train)
rf_classifier.fit(X_train, Y_train)
bagging_classifier.fit(X_train, Y_train)
ada_boost_classifier.fit(X_train, Y_train)
gradient_boosting_classifier.fit(X_train, Y_train)
xgb_classifier.fit(X_train, Y_train)
performance_metrics = {"Model": [], "Train Accuracy": [], "Test Accuracy": [], "Train F1-score": [], "Test F1-score": [], "Train Precision": [], "Test Precision": [], "Train Recall": [], "Test Recall": []}
def evaluate_model(model, model_name):
    train_pred = model.predict(X_train)
    test_pred = model.predict(X_test)
    performance_metrics["Model"].append(model_name)
    performance_metrics["Train Accuracy"].append(accuracy_score(Y_train, train_pred))
    performance_metrics["Test Accuracy"].append(accuracy_score(Y_test, test_pred))
    performance_metrics["Train F1-score"].append(f1_score(Y_train, train_pred))
    performance_metrics["Test F1-score"].append(f1_score(Y_test, test_pred))
    performance_metrics["Train Precision"].append(precision_score(Y_train, train_pred))
    performance_metrics["Test Precision"].append(precision_score(Y_test, test_pred))
    performance_metrics["Train Recall"].append(recall_score(Y_train, train_pred))
    performance_metrics["Test Recall"].append(recall_score(Y_test, test_pred))
evaluate_model(dt_classifier, "Decision Tree")
evaluate_model(rf_classifier, "Random Forest")
evaluate_model(bagging_classifier, "Bagging")
evaluate_model(ada_boost_classifier, "AdaBoost")
evaluate_model(gradient_boosting_classifier, "Gradient Boosting")
evaluate_model(xgb_classifier, "XGBoost")
performance_df = pd.DataFrame(performance_metrics)
print(performance_df)
